findings.F1: The test's result points the way the idea predicts but stays short of the bar. On all folds the mean short-direction unusual 5-day move is +0.67 % with t 1.00 (1055 cases, 390 days). On folds B and C it is +2.10 % with t 1.91 (297 cases, 135 days). The test already used every coin and fold available on daily bars, so there is no more data to add.
findings.F2: The effect sits in the deepest falls only.
findings.F3: At the plan's 5-day horizon the size of the forecast does grade the move (slope 0.0036, correlation 0.20). At 1 and 2 days it does not (correlation 0.06 and -0.01). The 1- to 2-day moves are just as large (+1.53 % t 2.04, +1.61 % t 2.01), but they are ungraded. So the 5-day horizon is where the graded effect shows.
findings.F4: The effect also swings with the period, and the market's moves add noise.
findings.F5: Agitation does not separate the result clearly. Agitated cases give +3.52 % (t 1.67) and calm cases +1.67 % (t 0.61). Agitated cases are only 18 of 297, so no profile narrowing is supported.
findings.F6: Even the full idea's total move per case (-0.15 %) is below the 0.22 % cost of a trade. A book can only pay on the larger moves of the deepest-fall cases (+4.6 % unusual in F2).

ideas.idea: When a coin's daily close sits near the top of that day's high-low range after a 5-day fall larger than the coin's usual 5-day move, in a falling market, its price falls over the next five days, and the deeper the 5-day fall, the larger the fall that follows.
ideas.consequence: A trader shorts high closes only after unusually deep 5-day falls in a falling market, where the follow-through is several times the cost of a trade, and leaves the shallow-fall cases alone.
ideas.name: high close after deep fall
